form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Heinrich (for himself and Ms. McSally) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs

form.official-title: To allow Homeland Security Grant Program funds to be used to safeguard faith-based community centers and houses of worship across the United States, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Faith-Based Community Center Protection Act.

section.header: Amendment to Homeland Security Grant Program
section.text: Title XX of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 601 et seq.) is amended—

subparagraph.text: by redesignating paragraphs (10) through (14) as paragraphs (12) through (16), respectively;
by redesignating paragraphs (6) through (9) as paragraphs (7) through (10), respectively;
by inserting after paragraph (5) the following:

paragraph.text: The term faith-based community center means—

subparagraph.text: a facility operated by a nonprofit faith-based community organization for the provision of recreational, social, or education services; or
by inserting after paragraph (10), as so redesignated, the following:

paragraph.text: The term nonprofit means an organization described under section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 and exempt from tax under section 501(a) of such Code.

clause.text: in paragraph (13), by striking and at the end;
by redesignating paragraph (14) as paragraph (15); and
by inserting after paragraph (13) the following:

paragraph.text: protecting a faith-based community center or vulnerable populations, including children or the elderly; and

subparagraph.text: by adding at the end the following:

subsection.header: Protection of faith-Based community centers and vulnerable populations

paragraph.text: Of the total amount authorized to be appropriated under paragraph (3) for grants awarded for the purpose described in subsection (a)(14), the Administrator shall award—

subparagraph.text: 50 percent for the protection of faith-based community centers and vulnerable populations in communities with a population of not more than 1,000,000 individuals, as determined by the latest available decennial census; and

50 percent for the protection of faith-based community centers in communities and vulnerable populations with a population of more than 1,000,000 individuals, as determined by the latest available decennial census.

paragraph.text: There are authorized to be appropriated $75,000,000 for fiscal year 2020 to the Administrator to make grants for the purpose described in subsection (a)(14).

section.text: Section 1038(a)(1)(A) of title 18, United States Code, is amended by striking 5 years and inserting 10 years.
